area: Raw and finished CAD geometry extraction
formula: finished geometry measured by OCCT; raw geometry not accepted
assumptions: the STEP is the finished part (stated in forging.ts:597-599 and machining-time.ts:546-552)
evidence: Recorded OCP measurements in tests/fixtures/real-parts-baseline.json re-used for all probes; OCP installed and the kernel re-read the STEP files in probes P2/P3. No input exists for an as-cast/as-forged CAD.
notes: Finished geometry measurement is the strongest part of the chain; raw geometry is derived (see machining allowance).

formula: as-cast = finished + Σ(holes ≤ Ø20 drilled-from-solid volume) + Σ(face-row area × stock) + Σ(cored-bore π·D·L × stock) + turned area × stock; as-forged = finished + holes ≤ Ø25 + face stock (IS 3469 by greatest dimension) + 2 mm turning stock + draft metal Σ A·h·tanα/2
inputs: finished volume × grade density (measured); feature table (measured); stock per side (constant / IS 3469 table); draft angles IS 3469 Table 1.4
assumptions: uniform stock on every machined face; parting plane at mid-extent; every hole ≤ Ø20 (cast) / ≤ Ø25 (forged) drilled from solid
evidence: Hand re-calc, Casting_Braket: 2.512 kg + (12.68 cm³ holes + 18,166 mm² × 3 mm = 54.5 cm³) × 0.00785 = 3.039 kg — matches costed 3.039. Knuckle forging 2.795 → 3.848 kg (+37.6 %); MODELLED yoke 1.433 → 2.316 kg (+61.6 %, mostly stock on 22 non-machined planar faces, P2/P4-C). Arithmetic closes; the inputs (which faces, how much stock) are unreliable.
notes: The screen form can take a typed as-cast / as-forged weight (single number); headless cannot.

code: calculator/src/engine/machining-time.ts:379-390 (CAST_MACHINING_STOCK_MM = {sand_ferrous 3.0, sand 2.0, gravity 1.5, investment 1.0, hpdc 0.5}); forging.ts:265-292 (closed-die IS 3469 Table 1.5: ≤205 1.5, ≤410 2.5, ≤610 3, ≤915 4, else 5 mm; other routes unsourced); machining-time.ts:695-696 (NEAR_NET_TURN_STOCK_MM 2 mm, unsourced)
formula: one per-side figure for every machined face and bore of the part
assumptions: casting value labelled "ISO 8062-3 RMA typical for 100–250 mm"; basis text concedes it is RMA + ½ DCTG "assumed, not read"
evidence: P4-A: bracket stock 1.5/3/4.5/6 mm → £10.405/£10.718/£11.032/£11.345 (±2.9 % per 1.5 mm) with machining-centre minutes unchanged at 4.73 min — stock moves weight only. PRCR002 ±3.2 %. No size dependence for castings, no DCTG/EN 10243-1 tolerance term, no roughing v finishing split, no per-feature value, no drawing input, no "insufficient stock" check.
notes: ISO 8062-3 RMA depends on the casting's largest dimension and the RMA grade; the code uses one value per process.

code: calculator/server/utils/cad-geometry-engine.py:354 (min_face_area 400 mm²), :441-446 (face rows = the 8 largest distinct planar areas); calculator/src/engine/feature-machining.ts:120-123 (defaultInclude near_net = every hole + every face row); feature-machining.ts:173 (lands), steppedBoreGroups :192-230
formula: machined set = all holes + top-8 planar-area buckets ≥ 400 mm², any orientation; pockets / bosses off
assumptions: "a near-net casting's large planar faces exist to be faced; as-cast surfaces are draft walls, not flats" (feature-machining.ts comment)
evidence: P2 (OCP re-read): MODELLED yoke face rows = 22 faces incl. 8 drafted walls (normal z-component ±0.087 = 5° draft) and 8 inner/outer I-beam flange faces; its source script (FORGE_modelled_parts.py) says only the eye faces and bores are machined. P4-C1: costing only the 4 eye faces → £16.83 → £10.18 (−39.5 %). Bracket has exactly 8 face rows (the cap). Pocket floors appear as both pocket and face rows (bracket 1839 mm², Part1 2915/1986 mm²). Holes: stepped-bore grouping and lands verified in op text (PRCR002 "3 cored bores, 3 stepped").
notes: Hole recognition is good; face (machined-surface) recognition is a heuristic with no drawing, draft or datum input. Engineer ticks exist on the casting/forging FORMS only (main.ts:11180), not headless.

formula: ops = one "Finish machining — <dir> side" per kernel direction (time = millMin × share of ALL B-rep faces in that direction) + one drilling op + one finish-boring op + slitting + lathe op + handling + bench deburr/gauge
evidence: Bracket ops: +Z 1.476, +X 0.954, +Y 0.708 min — shares 108/70/52 of all 230 faces, not of the 8 machined faces. No OP10/OP20 numbering (except a lathe op NAME "op 10 / op 20"), no datum, no feature-to-op tolerance link, no tool list per op. Hub flange: Ø60 bore finish-bored on the 5-axis mill, separate from the lathe op that turns the OD (concentricity datum not held); lathe "op 10 / op 20" charged ONE load (£0.456 before OH/margin).

formula: rank split-3axis (setups = dirs + drill), consolidated-5axis (1 setup near-net), volume-cell HMC (≤4 dirs → 1 clamping) by machine + operator £/part
inputs: cut minutes, direction count, bbox, batch, volume
assumptions: a 4th-axis tombstone reaches any ≤ 4 directions; a 5-axis reaches every side of a near-net part in one clamping
evidence: Alternatives ARE priced (bracket: HMC cell £2.26 v 5-axis £2.84 v split £3.20). But P3: a single rotary axis cannot reach the costed features of the bracket (7 approach directions incl. ±Z, ±Y, −X, inclined), PRCR002 (8), knuckle (9) or Part1 (11) — each needs ≥ 2 clampings; all were costed in 1. 5-axis "1 setup" ignores opposite machined faces (+Z and −Z on the bracket). Envelope checked; part weight, fixture complexity, tolerance capability not.

area: Number of setups and fixture requirements

code: calculator/src/engine/machining-time.ts:118 (SETUP_MIN_PER_FIXTURING 45), :99-107 (handling by weight), :115 (tool change 2.2 s, sourced), :397-432 (nearNetMachiningTime), :503-522 (turning); feature-machining.ts:145-147 (allowances), featureTime :362-436; cutting-catalogue.ts (sourced vc/fz/f rows), :240-248 faceMillCutMinutes; cast-and-machine.ts machiningOperationInputs (setup ÷ batch); routing-optimiser.ts:97 (batch = annual/20, 50–5000)

inputs: makers' cutting data (sourced, cutting-catalogue.ts rows); allowances, handling, setup, deburr (engineering-typical, unsourced, labelled)

No probing, no in-process gauging, no tool-life change time, no rapid model beyond fixed allowances.
